summary: Sporting News assesses possible replacements for Erik ten Hag should Manchester United sack him after a Champions League group-stage exit and a poor defensive record. It weighs candidates such as Zinedine Zidane, Graham Potter, Roberto De Zerbi, Michael Carrick, Hansi Flick, Antonio Conte and Julen Lopetegui, and dismisses Nagelsmann, Scaloni, Southgate and Pochettino as unlikely. It also lists United's managers since Sir Alex Ferguson, with Jim Ratcliffe's new 25% stake adding pressure.
one_line: Sporting News ranks the realistic and unrealistic candidates to replace Erik ten Hag at Manchester United if he is sacked in December 2023.
key_facts: Manchester United lost 1-0 to Bayern Munich on the final day of Champions League group play and finished bottom of their four-team group, their worst showing in the competition since 2005.
United conceded 15 goals in six games, a record for most goals against in a Champions League group stage by an English club.
United sit eighth in the Premier League, and their -5 goal difference is the worst of any club in the top 10.
Jim Ratcliffe completed his investment after a year of negotiations, taking 25% of his boyhood club, and wants United back at "the very top of world football".
Zinedine Zidane, 51, has been out of work since leaving Real Madrid in 2021 and told Marca in June 2022 he was not thrilled about a Premier League job because of the language barrier.
Roberto De Zerbi, 44, led Brighton to the Europa League for the first time in club history.
Michael Carrick made 316 appearances for United over 12 years and manages Middlesbrough, who are 11th in the Championship, three points off the playoff spots.
Carrick was United's caretaker manager in 2021 after Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's dismissal, before Ralf Rangnick took over.
Hansi Flick won the treble with Bayern Munich in 2019/20, was named UEFA Coach of the Year, and lasted only two years as Germany manager.
Antonio Conte has been out of work since leaving Tottenham in the summer, and the article says he seems to prefer working in Italy.
Julen Lopetegui, 57, left Wolves days before the current season amid tension with the board, similar to leaving Spain just before the 2018 World Cup.
Julian Nagelsmann, Lionel Scaloni, Gareth Southgate and Mauricio Pochettino are listed as names that don't make sense; Southgate's England contract expires in December next year.
The next United manager would be the ninth coach since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in May 2013, counting caretakers Ryan Giggs, Ralf Rangnick and Carrick.
